Changes since v2.1.1:

- Theorem 7.6 raises the lower bound for f(n) from 13n/24 to 11n/20. Write n + 1 = 20q + r with 0 ≤ r ≤ 19 and put e = 1 if r ≥ 12, else e = 0; then every 2-colouring of 2^[n] has a red and a blue sublattice with n + 1 + 2q + e members in total. The proof stacks windows of twenty levels. The window (Lemma 7.7: every 2-colouring of 2^[19] has a red and a blue sublattice with 22 members in total) is reduced by hand to 5,308,416 patterns, which four independent programs in C, C++, Python and Julia check from an explicit list of 63,272 sublattices (`checks/window20/`). Lean checks the colourings by size (`W20.splits_card19`); the hand reduction and the patterns with mixed levels are not formalised.
- Proposition 5.5: for n ≥ 206 and 1 ≤ N ≤ 2^{n/4} there are at least 2^{N−1} union-closed families of N subsets of [n], so the counting criterion gives no bound on F(n) below 2^{n/4} and Question 9.2 has a negative answer. It is proved in Lean (`CountFails.lean`). The negative answer was first given in the trureturing repository (commit `c0bb36b`, 9 October 2026), which the paper credits.
- The paper cites P. Chojecki's note of 18 March 2026, which proved the second conjecture first, as F(n) ≤ n^{log₂ n + O(log log n)}, and also gave f(n) ≤ (3 + o(1)) n log₂ n.
